title: This week · Tell a family-life story
description: Practise speaking about a small mix-up or change of plan, then write the clearest version of your story. A made-up story is fine. No deadline has been set yet.
objectives: Tell four connected past events and explain why something happened.
Notice and improve two useful verb choices.
source: Original Rory’s English practice linked to English in Context 5, Unit 1: Family life (pp. 20–25); not a textbook exercise.

tasks.prompt: 1 · Plan (3 minutes). Think of a real or invented time when someone in a family or group misunderstood a plan. Write five keywords: who, where, what each person thought, what happened, and how they solved it. You may use a friend instead of a family member.

2 · Speak (8 minutes). Open Speaking studio and choose “Tell a story”, or simply record a rehearsal there. Tell your story for about one minute without reading full sentences. Say at least four things that happened in the past, then explain the misunderstanding with because. Listen to your rehearsal or think back over it. Try again, improving two past verbs. The rehearsal stays on your device; no audio file is attached here. In this box, note two verbs you improved and one thing you said more clearly.

3 · Write and send (9 minutes). Write your improved story in 5–7 complete sentences. Include at least four past events, a reason with because, and one question the people could ask next time to avoid the mix-up. Optional start: “Last Saturday, …”. Check that you used past forms for past events. Then press Send answers to Rory.

title: Next week · An email about a family weekend
description: Start this next week. Practise the informal-email format from Unit 1 and tell a friend about a weekend plan. A fictional family is fine. This is a shorter first draft towards the book’s roughly 200-word email task; no deadline has been set yet.
objectives: Organise an informal email for a friend.
Use past verbs for an event and present forms for a usual routine.
source: Original Rory’s English practice linked to English in Context 5, Unit 1: Family life (especially p. 25); shorter practice draft, not the textbook exercise.

tasks.prompt: 1 · Say your ideas first (4 minutes). Tell an imaginary friend what your family or a made-up group usually does at the weekend, then describe one thing that happened last weekend. Try one “usually” sentence and two “last weekend” sentences aloud. You can use Speaking studio’s “Everyday conversation” or practise by yourself. The recording stays on your device; no audio file is attached here. Write your three best spoken sentences in this box.

2 · Write (16 minutes). Write a 120–150-word first-draft email to an imaginary friend about family life. Use a greeting and friendly ending. Say what your family or invented group usually does, tell a short story about last weekend in the past tense, and explain one thing you like or would change. Use because and one other linking word. This shorter draft helps you work towards the book’s roughly 200-word task; it is not the full school-length email.

3 · Check and send (5 minutes). Reread your email. Copy one past-tense sentence and one “usually” sentence, then improve them if needed. Check the greeting, ending and paragraph breaks. Finish with “I worked independently” or name any help you used. Then press Send answers to Rory.
